statement.p: Calculate the directional derivative of f(x,y)=xy in the direction u of \mathbf{v}=3 \mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} at the point P=(2,-1). Remember to normalize the direction vector.

static.solution:
\mathbf{v} to obtain a unit vector \mathbf{u} in the direction of \mathbf{v}: \mathbf{u}= rac{\mathbf{v}}{||\mathbf{v}||}= rac{1}{\sqrt{10}}(3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}) We compute the gradient of f(x,y)=xy at the point P: 
abla f=\left\lt  rac{\partial{f}}{\partial{x}},  rac{\partial{f}}{\partial{y}} ight>=\left\lt y,xight>\quad \Rightarrow \quad 
abla f(2,-1)=\left\lt -1, 2ight> The directional derivative in the direction \mathbf{v} is thus D_uf(2,-1)=
abla f(2,-1) \cdot \mathbf{u}=\left\lt -1, 2 ight> \cdot  rac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \left\lt 3, -1ight>= rac{-5}{\sqrt{10}}\approx -1.58114
